subject: Texas AI Docket, Carousel No. 17, September 6th, 2026, Two doors. Different latches.
body:
Two doors. Different latches.

Carousel No. 17, September 6th, 2026

Did NOT meet the bar: 6.552 against 6.8. Read before posting.

This run did not merge, so the images below come from the run branch claude/daily-2026-09-06 rather than from main. They stop resolving if that branch is deleted.

PANELHOLD. Median 6.552 against 6.8, one hard fail from the reader on slide 1's dek
prompt_auditPASS, 1383 tool calls measured, none waited on a human

What degraded

  • THE DECK DID NOT SHIP. Five scoring rounds, panel median 6.552 against a 6.8 bar, and one hard fail. A hard fail stops the deck at any round whatever the median is.
  • The hard fail was NOT repaired, deliberately. A run that fixes a fault after the final round and then ships has graded its own repair. The branch carries the deck the panel actually read.
  • No merge. The pull request is open and ready and carries everything.
  • No variety ledger entries and no article page, because both exist for a deck that shipped.
  • Frame 3's letters cast at 135 degrees against the deck's stated 147. Measured three ways and recorded rather than papered over: a cast on the shallower azimuth bridges the mono side bearings into a strikethrough.
  • Frames 4 and 6 are no longer the same drawing in type but remain the same camera class, and the last three frames are still dark in a row. Both were named by judges and neither was repaired.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it Two doors. Different latches., paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

Two routes. One veto.

A new charter needs the education commissioner's recommendation first. The State Board of Education can refuse it. That board has refused. Education Freedom Accounts publishes four requirements instead. A child carries $10,474 to an approved private school.

Alpha School's front page says an AI tutor gives students their coursework. ProPublica and The Texas Tribune report the board rejected Alpha's charter pitch last summer. The program accepted most of its campuses anyway.

A spokesperson for the voucher program told them "That wasn't relevant." Read the four requirements and that answer holds up. Not one of them asks who or what does the teaching.

Alpha's own front page says its classes learn twice as fast and names no study. Which of the four would ever check whether it works?

#EducationFreedomAccounts #TexasSBOE #AlphaSchool

2. The first comment

Sources, official records and first party accounts. The last date on each line is the date this run fetched the document. Any earlier date in a line belongs to the document itself, to its title or to what it covers.

The absences this deck publishes are measured against a named document rather than asserted. a1, a complete sentence inventory of the program's Schools page found no sentence concerning curriculum, instructional method or who does the teaching. a2, repeated passes over Alpha School's front page found no study, no test name, no footnote and no asterisk behind either performance figure. a3, the state's charter release for last year contains no occurrence of Alpha School, of Alpha or of 2hr Learning, so this deck draws no line between that release's named vetoes and this school.
The full record, every claim and every source. https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0125/

The machine changed itself

  • verbatim_check gained a third direction: a dossier that declares a TRUNCATION of what the frame prints now fails.
    Frame 4 declared 'Be located in Texas' while the frame printed claim c5 whole. Both existing tests are containment tests, so both passed, and the gate only ever held the DECLARED string to the record. The eleven words a reader receives were never checked against anything while the receipt read clean. Round 4 had hard failed this deck for truncating that same claim, the frame was repaired and the plan was not.
  • quantifier_check gained a fourth rule: a CLOSURE must name its set, the way a universal already must.
    The round 5 hard fail passed four gates, each right about its own question. numeral_lint traces 'two' to a computation, aggregate_check has the count declared, absence_check reads negations and there is none, and the universal rule wants a quantifier word and a set noun off two lists holding neither. What makes the sentence false is 'The other'.
  • shipped_check gained a HELD case, so a run that did not publish is out of scope rather than a defect in published work.
    CI could not go green on this branch: the sweep reports problems in work that is ALREADY PUBLISHED and read a run directory as proof of publication, so it reported the completion gate's own 'THE DECK DID NOT SHIP' as a defect. Nothing is dropped, every finding is still printed as a note. The first draft tested ship: false and put four PUBLISHED decks out of scope, so the test is a non-empty hard_fails list instead, and the self-test was watched go red on that exact mistake.
  • A gate for an undeclared NEGATIVE was REFUSED, with two measurements over every shipped deck.
    Requiring a negation-bearing sentence to cite a numbered absence fires on 136 of 136 negatives, because absence ids in a citation rail are a habit this run started and sixteen decks do not have them. Tightening absence_check from 'does this frame name a document' to 'does this sentence' adds 58 findings of the form 'It states no total.' A wall is not a gate. Both tables are in the backlog so the next phase starts from them.
  • PROPOSAL: render.py should capture window.__txProbe into the render report.
    Nine frames set a probe and the report has no field for it, so two acceptance items claiming a number was 'printed to the render report' had never been true of any deck. Fixed inside the frames for now by making 5 and 8 THROW rather than render. The real fix is three lines in a file under .claude/, which no routine may write.
  • PROPOSAL: site_build.py should decline the article page for a run whose score.json says ship is false.
    It writes an article page for any date with run artifacts, so this held deck has one committed carrying the sentence the panel hard failed, and site_fresh_check then forbids deleting it. Only the no-merge rule keeps it off the live site.
  • PROPOSAL: docket_build --validate accepts a numeral traced to a key_date the same run typed.
    Two dates on the Tesla item satisfied the numeral gate on the strength of a field nobody fetched. CI caught the consequence rather than the cause.
  • PROPOSAL: verbatim_check and quantifier_check self-tests are in guards.yml in no form.
    Filed 2026-09-04 and still true, and it costs more now that both carry a corpus calibration reading every shipped deck that CI has never run.

Each reverts on its own commit.

Notes

THE RECORD SHIPPED AND THE DECK DID NOT. Both halves are true and neither excuses the other. The record. Eleven items came due and were re-verified, seven re-worded with movement notes and four re-fetched by hand, none rotten. Four new items were admitted, 108 to 112: the Education Freedom Accounts requirement list for private schools, ERCOT's Batch Zero classification notice, the Department of Information Resources' account of the four AI laws the 89th Legislature passed, and Tesla's registration of an Austin semiconductor fab with the licensing department. Five sentences over the 30 word backstop were split in the ledger rather than in the build, because a generated page can only be fixed at its source. Every site gate exits 0 across 678 pages. The deck is HELD. Five scoring rounds, panel median 6.552 against a 6.8 bar, one hard fail. Slide 1's dek reads "Texas has two ways to put a school in front of a child on public money." It cites three claims and none of them enumerates the routes, and the sentence closes the set, which is false on the plain reading because a zoned district school arrives by neither route. The scope limit was written down the whole time, in aggregates.json, saying the count is "never a claim that Texas has no other way of funding a school". It was in a JSON file. The frame is where a reader is. EVERY HARD FAIL IN THIS RUN WAS ONE SPECIES and it took five rounds to see it. A sentence asserting a negative, or closing a set, that no claim and no absence measures. Round 2 on slide 1, round 3 on slide 5, round 3 and round 4 in the first comment, round 5 on slide 1 again for a different reason. Four rounds repaired the sentence a judge named and shipped the next one. The fault is a one sentence fix and it is NOT applied. A run that repairs a hard fail after the final round and then ships has graded its own repair, which is the exact failure this project's scoring contract was rewritten to prevent. The branch carries the deck the panel read. Machine QA is zero fails on all nine frames and every deck gate exits 0. The hold is a judgement about a sentence rather than a gate going red, which is what the panel is for.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck did NOT merge, so nothing here is on main and there is nothing to post. The links resolve against the run branch for as long as it exists.
